📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

One of German football’s most historic rivalries returns this Sunday as Werder Bremen host Hamburg at the Weserstadion in the 111th Bundesliga edition of the Nordderby. With just three points separating the two clubs, the encounter promises to be one of Matchday 10’s most fascinating fixtures.

Recent findings suggest that bremen enter the match sixth with 15 points, while Hamburg sit 11th with 12. Both clubs have enjoyed encouraging spells this season, making the derby particularly significant beyond their historic rivalry.

Daniel Thioune – who signed an extension 24 hours prior to the derby – has transformed Bremen into a more competitive side, with their seven-match unbeaten run ending against VfB Stuttgart before the international break.

Recent findings suggest that the Weserstadion has become a major advantage. Bremen remain unbeaten there this season, collecting 10 points from four matches. Niclas Füllkrug has been instrumental in their resurgence, scoring nine Bundesliga goals in nine appearances.

Hamburg, meanwhile, have struggled away from home, losing four of their five matches on the road. However, their recent 3-1 victory over Borussia Mönchengladbach demonstrated their attacking potential, particularly through Miro Muheim’s dangerous long-range shooting.

Recent findings suggest that the Nordderby also presents an intriguing managerial storyline. Thioune previously coached Hamburg and worked alongside current Hamburg head coach Merlin Polzin at Osnabrück before their paths crossed again in Hamburg.

According to recent reports, history favours Bremen, who have won eight of their previous nine Bundesliga home encounters against their northern rivals. Last season, however, both clubs won their respective home derbies, highlighting the unpredictable nature of this fixture.

Sources indicate that for Bremen, victory would reinforce their European ambitions and demonstrate that their impressive start is sustainable. Hamburg, meanwhile, have an opportunity to move level on points with their rivals and strengthen their position in the Bundesliga.

It has been revealed that regardless of their respective league positions, the Nordderby represents something much bigger than three points. It is a contest shaped by history, regional pride and the desire to establish supremacy in northern Germany.

With both teams showing encouraging signs this season, Sunday’s encounter has all the ingredients to deliver another memorable chapter in one of the Bundesliga’s greatest rivalries.

Harry Kane’s surgery likely to force Bayern Munich’s hand on January 2027 transfer market

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (784 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Getfootballnewsgermany

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, harry Kane’s serious injury has presented Bayern Munich with a problem that extends considerably beyond the loss of their leading striker.
  • In a recent development, kane underwent successful surgery overnight and is expected to remain sidelined well into 2027.
  • The question now concerns how Bayern intend to compensate for a player who functions simultaneously as a goalscorer, creator, and central reference point in Kompany’s system.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, harry Kane’s serious injury has presented Bayern Munich with a problem that extends considerably beyond the loss of their leading striker. The English international is expected to miss several months after suffering a syndesmosis ligament tear during Friday evening’s 1-1 Bundesliga draw against Cologne, leaving Vincent Kompany with an increasingly depleted collection of attacking options.

In a recent development, kane underwent successful surgery overnight and is expected to remain sidelined well into 2027. The Ballon d’Or winner has registered four Bundesliga goals and seven assists this season, making his absence particularly problematic given the considerable influence he exerts over Bayern’s attacking buildup.

The question now concerns how Bayern intend to compensate for a player who functions simultaneously as a goalscorer, creator, and central reference point in Kompany’s system. The increasingly uncomfortable answer is that a winter transfer may soon become unavoidable.

There is a certain irony surrounding Bayern’s current predicament. Get German Football News examined the club’s squad construction extensively in its 2026/27 Bundesliga tactical preview, noting that Bayern had repeatedly demonstrated an ability to function successfully with comparatively small squads. The German record champions entered the campaign with considerable attacking versatility, even if the options available to Kompany were not always distributed evenly across individual positions.

That flexibility has now been stretched to its limits.

It has been revealed that serge Gnabry and Ismael Saibari both sustained significant injuries during Bayern’s October encounter with Borussia Dortmund. The former is recovering from a hamstring problem and is not expected to return before the new year. Saibari suffered a syndesmosis injury of his own, requiring surgery and leaving him unavailable until well into 2027. Both would otherwise represent credible alternatives to Kane. Both Gnabry (Germany) and Saibari (Morocco) have experience operating as central attackers for their respective national teams.

Neither, however, is presently available to provide Kompany with a solution.

Jamal Musiala’s return against Cologne at least restores some attacking creativity, but the German international is only beginning to regain competitive rhythm after another lengthy injury absence. More importantly, Musiala is not a conventional striker and would be unlikely to replace Kane’s physical presence or finishing responsibilities.

Bayern must therefore look elsewhere.

Luis Diaz appears to offer the most plausible short-term answer. The Colombian is nearing a return from his thigh injury and could become available for Wednesday’s Champions League encounter against Lille. His extensive experience under Jürgen Klopp at Liverpool makes him an especially interesting candidate.

Industry observers note that during Klopp’s final season at Anfield, Diaz occasionally operated as a central attacker. Deploying Diaz centrally would nevertheless produce another problem. The Colombian has been Bayern’s principal left-sided attacking outlet. Removing him from that position would oblige Kompany to find another solution on the wing, particularly with Alphonso Davies still recovering from injury.

Nathaniel Brown has already demonstrated considerable positional flexibility, but asking the summer signing to assume yet another attacking assignment would hardly constitute an ideal long-term arrangement.

Lennart Karl represents another possibility.

The 18-year-old operated centrally after Kane departed against Cologne, occasionally exchanging positions with Tom Bischof. The youngster is not a natural centre-forward and stands at only five feet, six inches.

Industry observers note that his strengths lie in his technical ability, movement between the lines, and capacity to attack opponents while facing goal. Operating with his back to goal against physically imposing central defenders is an entirely different assignment.

According to recent reports, the remaining options are hardly reassuring. Nineteen-year-old Noah Codjo-Evora made his Bundesliga debut against Cologne, while highly regarded 16-year-old Bastian Assomo has attracted attention through his extraordinary goalscoring performances for Germany’s U17 national team.

It has been revealed that both are promising prospects, but neither should be expected to carry Bayern’s attacking responsibilities during a demanding Bundesliga and Champions League campaign. The shortage of established alternatives places sporting director Max Eberl in an increasingly difficult position.

Sources indicate that bayern have traditionally approached the winter transfer market cautiously, preferring to avoid expensive short-term solutions whenever possible. The prospect of injured players gradually returning after the winter break also provides a reasonable argument against making a hasty decision.

Sources indicate that A January addition would not necessarily have to be an expensive replacement for Kane. A versatile forward capable of operating centrally while providing cover across the attacking line could offer Kompany considerably greater flexibility without compromising the club’s longer-term aims.

Bayern may still find a way to cope without Kane over the coming weeks. Whether they can reasonably expect to do so for several months without additional reinforcements is an entirely different question.

At this stage, a January signing looks less like a luxury and increasingly like a necessity.

Mikey Moore reflects on conquering his nerves after Bundesliga breakthrough

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Tottenham Hotspur loanee Mikey Moore has expressed his relief after scoring his first Bundesliga goal in Friday evening’s 1-1 draw between Bayern Munich and FC Cologne.
  • Moore nevertheless displayed remarkable composure in the 12th minute at the Allianz Arena.
  • Sources indicate that the goal represented a significant breakthrough for an attacker whose performances had attracted mounting criticism during his first months in Germany.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tottenham Hotspur loanee Mikey Moore has expressed his relief after scoring his first Bundesliga goal in Friday evening’s 1-1 draw between Bayern Munich and FC Cologne. The 19-year-old Englishman admitted afterward that his prolonged wait for a goal had left him concerned about how he might react when presented with a scoring opportunity.

Moore nevertheless displayed remarkable composure in the 12th minute at the Allianz Arena. After initiating an attacking combination involving Linton Maina and Noted El Mala, the youngster received the ball back from the latter, rounded Bayern goalkeeper Jonas Urbig, and finished confidently to give the visitors an early lead.

Sources indicate that the goal represented a significant breakthrough for an attacker whose performances had attracted mounting criticism during his first months in Germany. Moore subsequently came close to scoring again after halftime and contributed to several other promising attacking sequences.

Get German Football News awarded Moore its Player of the Match distinction and a 7/10 rating for his efforts against the German record champions.

Recent findings suggest that the performance came at an vital point in Moore’s Bundesliga development. As GGFN reported earlier this month, Cologne head coach René Wagner had continued to defend the Tottenham prospect despite inconsistent performances and several appearances on the substitutes’ bench.

Wagner repeatedly emphasized that Moore possessed the necessary attacking qualities to succeed in Germany, suggesting that a single decisive moment might provide the confidence required to establish himself.

Moore’s struggles subsequently prompted speculation that Tottenham might terminate his season-long loan during the January transfer window. Get German Football News examined the rumours and the considerable doubts surrounding an early recall following Cologne’s defeat to Bayer Leverkusen.

Friday’s performance provided welcome justification for that patience.

Moore covered 12.5 kilometres against Bayern, more than any of his Cologne teammates, and contested eleven individual duels. His attacking contributions also demonstrated the potential of a partnership that Wagner has been eager to develop.

GGFN first reported on the coach’s enthusiasm for a Moore–El Mala combination in September. The two youngsters have subsequently required time to develop an understanding, but their cooperation against Bayern produced some of Cologne’s most dangerous attacking moments.

Sporting director Thomas Kessler praised Moore afterward, emphasizing that the club had always recognized his potential despite the difficulties accompanying his adaptation to German football.

The 19-year-old nevertheless acknowledged that one successful performance would not be sufficient. Cologne remain without a Bundesliga victory in five matches, and both player and club will need to build upon their encouraging evening in Munich.

Industry observers note that “It was a really good feeling,” Moore – as quoted by Kicker – said after Friday’s match. “We combined really well, and then I tried to stay calm at the end. I hadn’t scored before, so I was afraid I might panic in front of goal.”.

Moore also discussed the developing understanding between himself and El Mala.

It has been revealed that “It takes a little time to understand each other perfectly,” the Englishman explained. “He’s extremely quick and loves making runs in behind the opposition defence.”.

Kessler praised the youngster’s development while emphasizing the importance of patience.

It has been revealed that “You could see why we signed him,” the Cologne sporting director explained. “Mikey has repeatedly shown promising signs. But if we want to be successful with young players, that takes time. It’s nice that Mikey was able to crown his performance with a goal, It’s a step in the right direction.”.

Moore himself remained determined to build on his breakthrough.

“I’ve settled in well,” the 19-year-old mentioned. “Now I have to back it up.”.

  • Recent findings suggest that musiala made his return as a substitute against Cologne, playing approximately 20 minutes after missing nearly two months with a thigh injury.
  • According to recent reports, the comments represent another development in a discussion that has increasingly occupied Bayern’s hierarchy.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that bayern Munich supervisory board member Karl-Heinz Rummenigge has defended recent comments from Uli Hoeneß and Jan-Christian Dreesen concerning Jamal Musiala’s long-term future, insisting that the club’s consideration of the German international’s health and lucrative contract is entirely normal. Speaking after Friday evening’s 1-1 Bundesliga draw against Cologne, the former Bayern CEO expressed support for his colleagues’ concerns and suggested that difficult financial decisions could eventually become necessary.

Recent findings suggest that musiala made his return as a substitute against Cologne, playing approximately 20 minutes after missing nearly two months with a thigh injury. Rummenigge nevertheless emphasized that it remained unclear whether the 23-year-old would recover his previous performance level.

According to recent reports, the comments represent another development in a discussion that has increasingly occupied Bayern’s hierarchy. Get German Football News previously reported on Uli Hoeneß’s concerns about Musiala’s ability to regain his previous form. Bayern CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen subsequently raised the possibility of discussions involving the midfielder’s family and representatives should his performances remain below expectations.

Musiala’s current contract runs through 2030 and could reportedly earn him as much as €30 million annually. Head coach Vincent Kompany addressed the situation at Thursday’s press conference, emphasizing that his responsibility was to maintain confidence in his players while respecting the different obligations of Bayern’s executives. Rummenigge, meanwhile, explicitly supported the club’s financial concerns.

The 71-year-old suggested that Bayern might eventually need to reconsider the financial arrangements surrounding Musiala’s contract if the midfielder proved unable to recover his previous level. He also expressed doubts that another club would be prepared to purchase Musiala under the present circumstances.

It has been revealed that nevertheless, Rummenigge emphasized that no immediate decision was necessary. Bayern would first observe how Musiala developed over the coming weeks before considering further steps.

“I know what you’re getting at, and I don’t think there’s anything scandalous about this at all,” Rummenigge told Sky Germany. “What Uli and Jan Dreesen noted was completely fine, in my opinion. When a club has to consider how to deal with that situation, I consider it responsible and completely normal.”.

In a recent development, “Unfortunately, what we know suggests that it will be difficult for him to return to the level he has so often demonstrated here in this stadium,” the former Bayern executive added. I can’t imagine Jamal leaving the club or another club buying him under these circumstances. That’s a problem.”.

In a recent development, “We’re all very interested in seeing him come back, ideally in top form,” Rummenigge concluded. “But what happens if that isn’t the case? Then we naturally have to consider the finances as well. We want to wait for now.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Il Napoli Primavera non va oltre l’1 a 1 casalingo contro il Perugia. Al termine del match ha parlato il tecnico della Primavera Antonio Nocerino, ecco le sue dichiarazioni:.

“Abbiamo fatto una buona gara, ma ci sono cose che a me non piacciono. Mi aspetto pochi errori e che non si sbaglia dalla gente tecnica, troppi errori nell’ultimo passaggio. La prestazione è buona, i ragazzi sono stati bravissimo, noi ieri l’abbiamo preparata che tanti erano in prima squadra. Abbiamo giocato contro una squadra che ha i punti che merita e gioca molto bene. Se andiamo a vedere la partita sono rammaricato, mi sono intristito, hai tante opportunità e non chiudi la partita, poi vabbè il rigore..sono cose che ci possono stare”.

Recent findings suggest that sulla fase difensiva: “Andando spesso uomo contro uomo, noi lavoriamo tanto sul doppio lavoro, cercando di mettersi a 1 metro e mezzo dalla distanza, sia per coprire palla nello spazio che essere pronti ad attaccare. Marotta? Al di là dell’espulsione è un giocatore molto importante per noi, dovrebbe essere più lucido nelle situazione di gara, ma questo fa parte della crescita e migliorare nella frenata e non andare di intuito, per portarlo dove vuoi tu. Ogni tanto capita l’errore, fa parte del percorso di questa stagione”.

Su Spinelli e Pereyra in prima squadra: “Sono contento e orgoglioso, vuol dire che il lavoro stanno facendo è giusto. Ma questo non basta, non bisogna accontentarsi, fare sempre qualche cosa in più; andare in prima squadra è bellissimo, poi bisogna farsi trovare pronto per stare più tempo e magari entrare, nel calcio non si può mai sapere”.

In a recent development, sulla Youth League: “Non siamo ancora come io vorrei, a volte devi accompagnare i ragazzi, che ancora non hanno vissuto il calcio dei grandi, piano piano stiamo cercando di fargli capire che devono essere pronti sempre. Sono bravi ragazzi e avere una mentalità forte li metterà in condizione di affrontare prime squadre. L’obiettivo è dargli autostima e meno negatività, cercando di aiutarli in questo percorso, non lasciarli abbattere. Le cose negative vengono, ma l’importante è reagire e quello è l’obiettivo che noi cerchiamo a livello emotivo”.

Sul Centro Sportivo: “Sicuramente deve alimentare l’entusiasmo, ormai sono tanti anni che vivo fuori e ho visto un pò tutto. A me dispiace è che si deve andare a vedere il negativo, quella cosa che non è costruttiva. Se io ho la possibilità e ho un presidente che cerca di fare qualcosa, io devo essere solo orgoglioso e onorato da napoletano, in modo che i napoletani non debbano andare via e possano avere la fortuna di essere in campi dove prepararsi fisicamente e mentalmente. Ormai quando uno fa c’è sempre qualcosa da dire, per Napoli è qualcosa che fa la differenza. Lo spero soprattutto per i ragazzi e per fargli coltivare il proprio talento. La cosa che mi sta deludendo è la negatività, non si guarda mai a chi vuole fare qualcosa di diverso che crede nella città. Chi non fa alla fine parla, deve solo parlare e buttare via l’aria alla bocca, io preferisco chi fa e alla fine sarà sempre criticato. Si tratta della mentalità italiana, c’è gelosia e invidia di chi vuole successo. A me questo dà fastidio, è un problema culturale, io nel mio piccolo sto cercando di andare avanti e non ascoltare la negatività, chi ti dirà che è facile ti sta mentendo. Mi auguro che il presidente faccia il centro sportivo, avere il centro sportivo è come l’aria”. Ecco il video:.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • A highly anticipated Bundesliga match between upstart clubs Elversberg and Freiburg has ended with Julian Schuster’s Breisgauer picking up all three points via a narrow 0-1 away victory over Vincent Wagner’s Elversberg.
  • Recent findings suggest that wagner made two changes to the team that lined up against Borussia Dortmund just prior to the international break.
  • In a recent development, neither team could be accused of being complacent in the opening ten minutes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A highly anticipated Bundesliga match between upstart clubs Elversberg and Freiburg has ended with Julian Schuster’s Breisgauer picking up all three points via a narrow 0-1 away victory over Vincent Wagner’s Elversberg. Freiburg – along with Niko Kovac’s Borussia Dortmund – have both taken advantage of record champions Bayern Munich dropping points against Cologne last night. Freiburg draw level with Bayern on points while Dortmund top the table after also narrowly edging out Borussia Mönchengladbach 0-1 away.

Recent findings suggest that wagner made two changes to the team that lined up against Borussia Dortmund just prior to the international break. Jan Gyamerah started at right back over Luca Sirch while Cole Campbell took the place of Germany U21 international Maurice Krattenmacher on the left wing. Schuster, meanwhile, employed just one change to the XI that began against Union Berlin 13 days ago. The star of that victory, Yuito Suzuki, was given a break after returning from international duty with Japan. German veteran Lucas Höler started in place of Suzuki in the No. 10 slot.

In a recent development, neither team could be accused of being complacent in the opening ten minutes. In point of fact, willingness to intensely engage in direct duels remained high on both sides. Amid the many changes in possession, however, neither team was able to achieve much of a breakthrough. Freiburg did win a pair of corners and Igor Matanovic came close to earning a chance in the 9th minute. It would nevertheless be unfair to say that the Breisgauer guests looked the better squad. Possession remained split down the middle throughout the first quarter-of-an-hour.

Sources indicate that elversberg won their first corner in the 18th minute thanks to some hard work on the dribble from Leverkusen loanee Francis Onyeka. The hosts were able to swing the ball into the box several times after the set-piece, yet couldn’t produce an effort on target. Maximilian Rohr and Lukasz Poreba managed to dig out another Elversberg corner in the 23rd minute. David Mokwa forced a stellar save from Mio Backhaus off the corner, but the Saarland hosts again failed to get the ball headed goal-ward on the successive dead-ball.

After the half-hour mark passed, the SVE began to look a tad more lively and creative. Gyamerah, Lukas Petkov, and Felix Keidel repeatedly got some solid attack charges going up the SVE right. The fact that the hosts gained an upper hand optically still produced little. Mokwa saw his attempt at a spectacular bicycle kick blocked in the 34th. Onyeka spurned a lovely play-in from Gyamerah in the 40th by losing the ball in the box. Apart from drawing a frustration-fueled yellow card out of Freiburg’s Jan-Niklas Beste, the promoted club had nothing to show for their efforts.

The match unquestionably maintained its intensity while undeniably featuring a steady loss of tempo.

Neither head coach opted to employ changes at the half. To the candid observer, these decisions were quite apparent. Schuster’s guests added a slight element of risk to their game, yet were still constrained by the fact that “paint the corner” passing around the box didn’t facilitate any danger. At the other end, Elversberg were gifted counter opportunities on both flanks in the opening ten minutes after the start, but noticeably lacked the pace to take true advantage of the accorded space. Onyeka came closest to creating a chance at the hour-mark, finding himself stymied centrally by a Maximilian Eggestein block.

The hosts eventually found themselves punished for failing to turn a slight optical advantage into a lead. Beste latched onto a long launch from SCF defender Philipp Lienhart in the 68th minute. After shielding the ball skillfully against SVE challenger Rohr, Beste actually inadvertently set up Igor Matanovic with a layoff. The Croat marksman nevertheless didn’t hesitate, reacting sharply to smack the ball deftly into the bottom right corner. Matanovic’s impressive ninth goal across all competitions this season gave the visiting Schwarzwälder a 1-0 lead.

With the deadlock finally broken, the encounter promptly became more entertaining. A Keidel-led counter-attack shortly after the opening goal nearly led to an equalizer, but SVE captain Lukas Pinckert ultimately shot wide. Not long after being subbed on, Suzuki thought he had doubled Freiburg’s advantage in the 76th minute. The goal was chalked off due to a narrow offside decision.

It has been revealed that plenty of action ensued for a time until Schuster’s men settled into a more compact block and the Freiburg coach sent on some attacking reinforcements. As the clock ticked on towards full-time, Freiburg looked the more likely team to score. Fresh SCF attackers Vincenzo Grifo and Keisuke Goto opened up more space in the SCF attacking third. Eggestein and Philipp Treu saw late tries for the 2-0 blocked.

Nicolas Kristof (5) – Jan Gyamerah (7), Lukas Pinckert (6), Maximilian Rohr (4), Lasse Günther (5) – Felix Keidel (7), Łukasz Poręba (5) – Lukas Petkov (6), Francis Onyeka (4), Cole Campbell (5) – David Mokwa (4).

Substitutes: Luca Sirch (5), Noel Futkeu (5), Tom Zimmerschied (5), Maurice Krattenmacher (6), Raif Adam (-).

Mio Backhaus (6) – Philipp Treu (5), Matthias Ginter (6), Philipp Lienhart (7), Jordy Makengo (4) – Maximilian Eggestein (4), Yannik Engelhardt (4) – Niklas Beste (6), Lucas Höler (3), Derry Scherhant (6) – Igor Matanovic (6).

Substitutes: Cyriaque Irié (5), Yuito Suzuki (6), Vincenzo Grifo (6), Keisuke Goto (6).

The Austrian central defender earns our distinction primarily for his decisive contribution to Freiburg’s winning goal. Lienhart’s expertly measured long ball in the 68th minute enabled Niklas Beste to break forward and ultimately set up Igor Matanovic’s finish. In a match largely characterized by midfield stalemates and limited attacking opportunities, Lienhart’s vision made the difference. The 30-year-old registered 74 touches, completed 83 percent of his 52 attempted passes, and covered 10.1 kilometres over the full 90 minutes. His impressive top speed of 32.2 km/h also deserves mention.

Industry observers note that freiburg striker Igor Matanovic believes his team’s newfound ability to grind out difficult victories represents a significant step forward under head coach Julian Schuster. Speaking to Get German Football News in the mixed zone after Saturday’s 1-0 Bundesliga victory over Elversberg, the Croatian international explained why Freiburg are now consistently collecting points in matches that might previously have ended in frustrating draws.

Matanovic’s 68th-minute winner against the promoted Saarland club extended Freiburg’s winning streak to five matches across all competitions. The latest success also moved Freiburg level on points with Bayern Munich near the top of the Bundesliga table.

Recent findings suggest that the 23-year-old believes Freiburg’s improvement reflects considerably more than a fortunate run of results. Matanovic emphasized the squad’s collective resilience, suggesting that the team’s current momentum has been built upon a healthy foundation and a willingness to discuss shortcomings openly.

The striker specifically recalled Freiburg’s response to three consecutive defeats earlier in the campaign, praising his teammates for refusing to allow the setbacks to undermine their confidence.

Sources indicate that saturday’s hard-fought victory provided another illustration of that mentality. As documented in GGFN‘s match report and player ratings, Freiburg struggled to create clear opportunities against a spirited Elversberg side before finally breaking through in the second half.

Matanovic explained that maintaining concentration and relying on familiar tactical principles were particularly vital in such circumstances. Aggressive pressing, collective defensive work, and persistence in winning possession eventually helped Freiburg create the decisive opening.

Industry observers note that “It’s tremendous. Obviously, it’s very nice to be collecting the points as well,” Matanovic stated when asked about Freiburg’s five consecutive victories. “I think that’s the difference compared to last season. What we were missing were the points. We often played well, but then we’d come away with just one point. Now we’re winning the dirty games.”.

In a recent development, “Even recently against Union Berlin, you know how unpleasant they can be to play against, and we still managed to win 2-0,” the Croatian continued. “There’s genuinely a very high level of quality in this team, and of course we’re enjoying a certain flow. But the flow we have comes from this healthy foundation that we can always rely upon. I often mention the three consecutive defeats we suffered. How many teams collapse after something like that? How many lose their confidence?”.

It has been revealed that “But we always get back to basics,” Matanovic went on. “We address things openly and honestly, and that’s how we find our way back into our flow. Right now, we’re simply very, very difficult opponents to face. You have to maintain your focus, especially when you’re not creating many chances or opportunities. Then you have these basics you can rely upon. Keep pushing forward, press high, make life difficult for the opposition, and block plenty of balls.”.

It has been revealed that “I think we also won possession back many times in the first half,” Matanovic concluded. “That’s something we force through our own efforts, and that’s how we eventually create scoring chances again. There weren’t many chances, but I think we could even have rewarded ourselves with more goals in the end.”.

It has been revealed that borussia Dortmund midfielder Felix Nmecha has refused to rule out repeating his controversial crown celebration despite previous assurances from Germany head coach Jürgen Klopp that the gesture would no longer be performed. Speaking after scoring the winning goal in Saturday’s 1-0 Bundesliga victory over Borussia Mönchengladbach, the 26-year-old defended his religious convictions while suggesting that the controversy surrounding his celebrations had been exaggerated.

Recent findings suggest that nmecha’s 80th-minute winner secured three crucial points for Niko Kovac’s side, sending Dortmund to the top of the Bundesliga table. The in-form German international has now scored five league goals this season, including three in his last two appearances. Nmecha’s most recent goal celebration till exhibited religious overtones, though the Dortmund professional did not repeat the crowning gesture that sparked the controversy in the first place. Nmecha spoke on the matter afterwards.

The controversy began following Dortmund’s 2-1 victory over SV Elversberg before the international break. Nmecha celebrated both goals by symbolically removing a crown and placing it on the ground. The gesture is associated with the evangelical football network Ballers in God, whose activities and reported positions on homosexuality and other social issues have attracted criticism.

Get German Football News previously reported on Dortmund’s response to the controversy, including objections raised by the club’s Fan and Supporters Department. Dortmund president Hans-Joachim Watzke subsequently appealed to Nmecha to reconsider the gesture, emphasizing the importance of avoiding unnecessary divisions among supporters.

According to recent reports, germany head coach Jürgen Klopp later indicated that the matter had been resolved following a personal conversation with Nmecha. Klopp explained that the midfielder had agreed not to repeat the celebration in its controversial form. Nmecha indeed opted for a different celebration after scoring against Gladbach, sliding towards the corner flag before kneeling and crossing his arms over his chest. After the full-time whistle, Nmecha dropped to his knees and engaged in prayer.

Industry observers note that dortmund sporting director Ole Book defended Nmecha’s right to express his Christian faith, distinguishing Saturday’s celebration from the gesture that had provoked criticism. Meanwhile, Ballers in God subsequently shared images of Nmecha’s latest celebration on social media, interpreting three of his gestures as symbolizing a direct communication of the player’s Christian faith.

“What people were saying didn’t ring true to me,” Nmecha told Sky Germany. “That celebration was simply about my faith, laying the crown on the ground for Jesus and giving him the glory. That doesn’t mean I’ll never do that celebration again.”.

Dortmund sporting director Ole Book also addressed Nmecha’s celebrations after the final whistle, defending the midfielder’s right to express his Christian faith. Book considered it legitimate for Nmecha to demonstrate his desire to thank Jesus and God for his goal, while emphasizing that the midfielder had refrained from repeating the controversial gesture.

“He didn’t perform the controversial part of the celebration today,” Book explained.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Recent findings suggest that the extraordinary scenes began before kickoff when the Bundesliga club announced that its stadium-wide sound system had suffered a technical failure.
  • At the request of the stadium announcer, who could still be heard faintly, supporters in Frankfurt’s Nordwestkurve began singing the club’s traditional anthem, Im Herzen von Europa, without any musical accompaniment.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that eintracht Frankfurt supporters provided one of the most heartwarming moments of Saturday’s Bundesliga action after a technical malfunction silenced the sound system at Deutsche Bank Park. Rather than allow the disruption to spoil the occasion, the Frankfurt faithful took matters into their own hands, providing their own musical accompaniment ahead of the Eagles’ 1-0 home victory over TSG Hoffenheim.

Recent findings suggest that the extraordinary scenes began before kickoff when the Bundesliga club announced that its stadium-wide sound system had suffered a technical failure. A message displayed on the stadium’s video screens warned supporters that the usual announcements and musical accompaniment would be unavailable until further notice. An unusually quiet atmosphere accompanied the players’ warm-ups. Frankfurt’s famously passionate supporters nevertheless had other ideas.

At the request of the stadium announcer, who could still be heard faintly, supporters in Frankfurt’s Nordwestkurve began singing the club’s traditional anthem, Im Herzen von Europa, without any musical accompaniment. The spontaneous performance proved particularly fitting given the song’s history. The beloved Eintracht anthem was originally recorded by Frankfurt’s police choir, whose rendition has become an integral part of the club’s home matchday tradition.

On Saturday, however, the supporters themselves assumed responsibility for the performance.

The club couldn’t resist making light of the unusual circumstances.

It has been revealed that “‘Im Herzen von Europa’, today performed not by the police choir, but by the stadium choir. That’s a first,” Eintracht observed in its matchday coverage. Nor did the impromptu entertainment stop with the anthem. Supporters also enthusiastically took over the team announcements, shouting out the starting lineup and providing a suitably rousing welcome as both teams emerged onto the pitch.

According to recent reports, the technical difficulties had threatened to deprive the afternoon of its familiar atmosphere. Instead, they had given the Frankfurt faithful an opportunity to demonstrate precisely why the Waldstadion remains one of German football’s most atmospheric venues.

Sources indicate that the singing continued into the opening stages of the match, with the Nordwestkurve providing vocal encouragement as Adi Hütter’s side sought to make the most of their home advantage. Frankfurt’s supporters were rewarded in the 25th minute when Jonathan Burkardt finished an excellent attacking move to give the hosts the lead.

Although faint goal music and an announcement could reportedly be heard amid the technical difficulties, the home fans hardly needed any encouragement to celebrate. There was further excitement before halftime when goalkeeper Noah Atubolu saved Andrej Kramaric’s penalty in the 41st minute. Frankfurt then received a spot kick of their own, only for Hoffenheim goalkeeper Oliver Baumann to deny Burkardt three minutes later.

According to recent reports, the stadium’s sound system was finally restored for the second half, but the supporters had already ensured that the unusual afternoon would be remembered for something considerably more enjoyable than a technical malfunction. Frankfurt ultimately protected their narrow lead to claim all three points, securing a third consecutive Bundesliga home victory.

Eintracht CEO Axel Hellmann was rather less enthusiastic about the technical difficulties. Speaking after the match, the club executive used the incident to renew his calls for a newly introduced stadium, pointing to increasingly frequent problems with the ageing arena’s electricity, lighting, and other infrastructure. Hellmann maintained that the situation would only deteriorate in the coming years and reiterated the need for a replacement venue, ideally completed by 2038.

Recent findings suggest that one can certainly appreciate Hellmann’s concerns. Nevertheless, there is a certain irony in the fact that the stadium’s shortcomings should become so apparent on an afternoon when its supporters demonstrated precisely what makes the place so special.

In a recent development, as Get German Football News noted in a feature on Germany’s most beloved traditional stadiums last November, the Waldstadion occupies a particularly cherished place in the hearts of the German footballing public. Nestled in the forest south of Frankfurt’s bustling financial district, the historic ground retains an identity that no corporate naming-rights agreement has ever managed to displace.

Whatever the future holds for the Waldstadion, Saturday’s events offered another reminder that the most important component of Frankfurt’s famous home atmosphere requires neither electricity nor expensive technology.

Just a few thousand willing voices.

In a recent development, bayer Leverkusen midfielder Malik Tillman has admitted that recent criticism from the club’s supporters has diminished his appreciation of their applause. Tillman assisted Afonso Moreira’s opening goal with an excellent pass and impressed with several further attacking contributions. When head coach Carles Martínez substituted the midfielder in the 67th minute, the BayArena crowd responded with enthusiastic applause and chants of his name.

According to recent reports, get German Football News previously reported on Tillman’s frustrations with Leverkusen supporters following a revealing interview with the Kölner Stadt-Anzeiger in August. Tillman also discussed difficulties with former coach Kasper Hjulmand and expressed disappointment over the support he had received from the club’s management.

In a recent development, the midfielder arrived from PSV Eindhoven in the summer of 2025 for approximately €35 million. Our detailed preseason assessment of Leverkusen highlighted Tillman’s difficulties establishing himself in Martínez’s prepares amid increased competition for attacking positions.

According to recent reports, saturday’s performance nevertheless offered fresh encouragement. Tillman demonstrated the technical quality and creativity that persuaded Leverkusen to invest heavily in his services. Whether the latest display will help repair his relationship with sections of the club’s support remains another matter.

Recent findings suggest that “I have confidence in myself, but playing a good game naturally strengthens that confidence even further,” Tillman explained after Saturday’s match, as reported by Kicker. “I have to keep going here, no matter what happens. But I’m happy with my performance.”.

Asked how he felt about receiving applause after previously being booed, the American offered a notably different response.

“It’s difficult to say at this point,” Tillman admitted. “I don’t really care anymore. I don’t know. Of course, it sucks when you get booed, and at the end of the day, it doesn’t really mean much to me anymore when people cheer or shout my name.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By LEWIS STEELE, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 19:01 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 08:25 EST, 16 November 2026.

Spending time in the tech giant of Neil Warnock is always an education, be it witnessing one of his legendary foul-mouthed touchline rants or perched at one of his stage shows at grand venues like London Palladium.

In a recent development, on this occasion, Daily Mail Sport is perched in an east London bar watching on as one of English football's national treasures is posing for some modelling. Yes, you read that right, Mr Warnock is here to launch his own pair of socks with a tipple of Famous Grouse whisky in hand.

The complements on Warnock's 77-year-old feet are soon over, though, and we can get on to talking about a life in football that started six decades ago as a winger for Chesterfield and has traversed 10 clubs as a player, 17 as a manager and more than 2,000 games in the dugout.

Sources indicate that so where to start? Maybe his reflections on nearly five decades in management – and how the whole conversation about feet is not too out of place….

Industry observers note that 'You don't realise how long it has been really, I started off just a team of ragamuffins as I call them,' he says in his iconic Yorkshire accent. 'They used to train on the green where I had digs in Hartlepool and asked me to coach them.

'I remember we scored from a set-piece we worked on, I was running up and down the touchline high-fiving everyone. I got the bug. I knew I could never get to the top as a player, I was quick but I was brainless.

Daily Mail Sport caught up with Neil Warnock to discuss his six decades in football.

After representing 10 different clubs as a player, Warnock became one of the most compelling managers in the game.

According to recent reports, 'I could've been a chiropodist if not in football. That could be on a quiz, couldn't it? I had bad feet at Scunthorpe, I used to get massive blisters so the physio there started getting me to do some of the players' feet.

'I enjoyed doing ingrown toenails and things like that! So I thought why not? Then I had a practice in Sheffield. I had to make a decision when we won the league at Scarborough whether to go full-time or pack it in. I thought, "Oh, go on then, let's give it a little go".

'It's not worked out badly, really, has it?

It has been revealed that 'People come up to me every day and say, "You're a legend, you". And I say, "Oh, thank you very much". Then they tell me what club they support, I have had so many haven't I? Last week I went out for a minute and had four selfies. They all appreciate what I did for their club.

Sources indicate that 'There aren't as many characters in the game now, you wouldn't get upset with managers now like in my day because now they are that b****y boring! Some of them barely speak.

'They won't get the rapport we had. I managed at a good time. The way I managed, I needed that humour. I needed the lads to enjoy it. I signed a lot of players that many managers wouldn't touch with a barge pole, are you with me? They ended up getting me promotions.'.

The aforementioned humour brings us on to a private conversation he had with the great Pep Guardiola, one of the millions of anecdotes up Warnock's sleeve but one that he has not told until now.

According to recent reports, 'I went to a training session and he asked me to say a few words,' explains Warnock. 'I remarked, "Well lads I bet you're glad I'm not your manager because we'd be kicking balls from there to there, chasing it, heading it, practicing our tackles"... everyone laughed.

Warnock views Pep Guardiola as the best manager of his lifetime, while the Spaniard praised the veteran's humour after once addressing his Man City squad at a training session.

Warnock has led teams to promotions on eight occasions over the course of his career.

Sources indicate that 'After the session we had a coffee and Pep remarked to me, "Neil, that was amazing, you know when you talked to the players? I understood why you had so many promotions".

'He started counting and remarked, "What we have is all these staff… computers, details, nutritionist, all these staff, but you know what we don't have? Humour". He noticed why my lads had done well in my teams, just in that meeting. It was good, that. He is amazing.

Sources indicate that 'Pep is the best manager of my lifetime. They say he had all the best players but it is not easy managing them. Pep did things with players and now there are non-league teams trying to play like Manchester City!'.

Warnock is now doing stage tours - Guardiola attended one last season - and had a tear in his eye when he stepped out at London Palladium given he used to watch shows there with his mother, who was in a wheelchair, on the TV as a child.

In a recent development, so what is Warnock up to these days? His current role is advisor at Torquay United but last management job was at Aberdeen two years ago… so is he out of the rat race for good this time?

In a recent development, 'No, not really, no,' he says. 'I only work from February to April! So the phone will be on after Christmas. You never know, do ya? There will be someone thinking "why don't we get that Warnock in?".

Industry observers note that 'I've retired 40 times! Every time I have stated it, I have meant it. But it's that dressing room camaraderie. There's something about football, when I look at some of the managers now… they just don't excite me.

'I remember Ruben Amorim (breaks down laughing). He's got his computer out on the bench! I remember watching and thinking, "I'm sorry, son, you need more than a computer to help you tonight!".

Warnock is currently doing stage tours, with Guardiola among the attendees last season.

Warnock's current role is advisor at Torquay United and briefly served as interim manager last season, with the 77-year-old admitting he had not completely ruled out a return to the dugout.

'And likewise, I see them making notes on the bench, oh my god. I think "what are you doing, your shopping list for Tescos?".

Sources indicate that 'I do enjoy walking and I enjoy photography, believe it or not. I go up the river with my phone, there's so many lovely things to see.

Recent findings suggest that 'I've got an electric bike and I sometimes do about 25 miles. I was thinking of doing a cycle of all my clubs but that would take me five years! They go at about 30mph down the hills, you've got to be careful, you wouldn't want to come off them.'.

He is also enjoying fishing, being with the family and playing golf with his son, a PGA rising star William - though Warnock Sr insists he often embarrasses himself playing off 'the ladies' tee'.

The thing that makes Warnock most proud is the four promotions at Wembley but also the togetherness he fostered in his many teams.

Recent findings suggest that he tells us: 'What I like about the teams I had, they all have reunions. You look at the tele now, someone will score a goal and kiss the badge… they won't have a reunion.

'When I go to these reunions, I see all my lads and how I blended that dressing room together and I look at the comradeship they still have now, they are the same as they were just a lot older.

It has been revealed that 'This year, my Scarborough team are having a 40-year celebration and the lads have invited me. I said there's no way I'm going out with that lot after the do because they can drink, let me tell you!'.

In a recent development, * The Famous Grouse has teamed up with Happy Socks to launch an exclusive limited-edition collection, available at Tesco stores across the UK. Shoppers can pick up a free pair of colourful, collectable socks with selected 70cl bottles of The Famous Grouse whisky, priced from £18.50. Available in-store only, while stocks last.

  • England ended world champions Spain's 43-match unbeaten run in dramatic fashion with a 3-2 win on a memorable night in Madrid.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CRAIG HOPE, CHIEF FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 02:32 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 09:25 EST, 16 November 2026.

England ended world champions Spain's 43-match unbeaten run in dramatic fashion with a 3-2 win on a memorable night in Madrid.

After Harry Kane, Ezri Konsa and Ben White scored to establish a three-goal lead, the visitors had to cling on after Elliot Anderson was sent off and the hosts scored twice in the final half hour.

The victory means Thomas Tuchel's side top their Nations League group and it provided a strong riposte to criticism of the manager following the World Cup semi-final defeat by Argentina in July.

Our chief football reporter, Craig Hope, was at the Metropolitano Stadium, and here are his FIVE substantial take-aways….

Industry observers note that it would not have mattered had England conceded a late equaliser. To draw comparison with Argentina in the final half hour is unfair and inaccurate. The World Cup semi-final was 11v11 and so, when we draw conclusions from this game, let us do so on the same terms.

Thomas Tuchel was delighted with his England players as they won 3-2 away in Spain.

Industry observers note that and what did England do at 11v11 with a 1-0 lead? They attacked. And attacked again. This was a major change (and improvement) and is the reason for such encouragement. They have learnt from a mistake, as much as Tuchel will be loathe to admit.

Sources indicate that mexico would be a fairer parallel, but that was against opposition far inferior to Spain. At 11v10, we could not expect England to stay on the front foot here, as they were until the point of Jarell Quansah's needless mistake and Elliot Anderson's subsequent red card.

And that is cause for great optimism - because this game was not in the balance in any way when the teams were at equal number.

For me, and I don't think this is even close, this was the best performance of Tuchel's reign.

Recent findings suggest that do England suddenly have a pair of full backs?! After years of trawling and trialling, here in the most testing of surrounds, Ben White and Lewis Hall inked their names into Tuchel's XI.

We can forgive the concession of two goals when down to 10 men - because with 11, Spain barely looked like getting a shot on target. In fact, they didn't.

According to recent reports, much of that was down to the solidity of the full backs. Then, with backs to the wall, the pair became bricks in the resistance. One White block late on was heroic.

Recent findings suggest that before that, Hall's best work was not in containing Lamine Yamal, but in emulating him. His dribbles were daring and unnerved Spain, who thought they would spend the game in England's half and with the ball. They did neither early on and Hall was central to that.

In a recent development, white's goal had shades of Carlos Alberto on the overlap, and his England redemption arc felt like it reached completion here. Let him now move on now, for England need him.

No more boos, please, only cheers for White (and Hall).

It's time to stop the boos for Ben White after he starred with Lewis Hall at full back.

According to recent reports, ezri Konsa is England's best defender. Build the backline around him.

Tuchel noted on the eve of the game that he thought Konsa had grown for the move to Arsenal, and this was proof.

Boy do England need a mature, reliable presence at the heart of their defence. Konsa revealed here why he can be that man. He scored a fine goal, which is always a sign of a defender ready to take wider responsibility, but it was his cool interceptions and desperate blocks at the other end that were most reassuring.

What Konsa has to do now is build on this - and a man-of-the-match performance at the home of the world champions is a pretty lofty and solid foundation from which to do so.

Tuchel will, and should, be giving serious thought to keeping James Trafford in England's goal for the Nations League quarter-finals.

Jordan Pickford has done nothing wrong. And yet, it feels like one position the manager wants to evolve - and here was his justification.

Industry observers note that trafford can be a little erratic and immature. What better way to grow, emotionally, than with a series of saves to preserve an historic win. He will feel like a different player, and person, to the one who started this game. Like White and Hall, this felt like a coming-of-age night in an England jersey.

Trafford has all the tools. He might just have used them to chisel his name into that team-sheet.

Goalkeeper feels like one position the manager wants to evolve - and James Trafford starred.

Spain's fans are left shocked as Ezri Konsa hails the brilliant Trafford in emphatic fashion.

Recent findings suggest that no goals, but England would not have won this game without Bellingham. He terrified Spain, perhaps given their intimate knowledge of his brilliance.

Beating the best is as much a mental challenge as it is physical, and Bellingham believed. He made England believe, too.

His swagger. His majesty. And yes, his skill. Of all the positives from this win, it is hard to look past Bellingham as the biggest reason for England being able to challenge Spain at the top of the world rankings.

Jude Bellingham played like a captain, dropping into midfield when down to 10 men.

He won the corner for the second goal and created the third. He then dropped into midfield when down to 10 and played like a captain.

In a recent development, that is what England need - Bellingham the leader, not Bellingham the individual. He has bought into the collective under Tuchel and, with that, his team-mates are buying into his big ideas. They don't come much bigger than what England achieved here.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Una conferma tra i pali. Doppio intervento salvifico, prima su N’Dri, poi su Guebbels. Prestazione di alto livello, in cui si dimostra di essere sempre pronto e attento quando viene in causa. Firma un altro clean sheet stagionale.

According to recent reports, cresce nel corso della gara, trovando nella ripresa maggiore incisività. Suo il cross per Taylor che porta all'azione del raddoppio laziale.

It has been revealed that meno preciso rispetto al compagno di reparto, alterna buoni interventi a qualche sbavatura di troppo. Si rende protagonista con il passaggio filtrante da metà area che porta alla doppietta di Noslin.

Industry observers note that prestazione di sostanza e grande attenzione in fase di marcatura. Sempre concentrato sulle azioni degli avversari, leggendo bene le situazioni.

Parte piano ma poi, con il passare dei minuti, sale di colpi continuando a sovrapporre sulla sinistra e contenendo bene N'Dri in difesa. Dal 78' Pellegrini - sv.

Ottima prestazione di sostanza, sfiora prima il gol con un colpo di testa sottomisura e poi segna con una perla, superando Falcone con un cucchiaio alla Boksic.

Tempismo e attenzioni sono i suoi punti di forza. Sempre puntuale nelle chiusure e preciso in marcatura. Si conferma una certezza quando c'è da arginare i pericoli degli avversari. Dall'83' Rovella - sv.

Sources indicate that il centrocampo senza di lui avrebbe tutt'altro volto. Il suo ordine e pulizia nella manovra sono ormai una certezza, ma partita dopo partita si conferma un pilastro di questa squadra. Prestazione brillante, impreziosita da un assist di tacco per Noslin alla Luis Alberto.

È incontenibile. Nell'avvio sembra accusare la stanchezza accusata dagli impegni con la Danimarca, ma riesce comunque a confezionare uno splendido assist per la rete del vantaggio. Nella ripresa si accende definitamente: le iniziative più pericolose passano da lui. Dal 78' Cancellieri 6,5 - Manda in porta Frattesi per il tris laziale.

Industry observers note that prezioso il lavoro al servizio della squadra. Libera spazi e si rende funzionale per i compagni. Meno incisivo in fase offensiva invece quando è chiamato a cercare qualche giocata individuale. Dall'88' Gudmundsson - sv.

È il vero leader di questo pomeriggio. Firma la sua prima doppietta stagionale, con un gol a tempo: prima un colpo di testa da vero numero nove, poi una conclusione di sinistro a tu per tu con Falcone. Dall'83' Dele-Bashiru - sv.

Industry observers note that la Lazio soffre un po' troppo nel primo tempo, ma lo chiude meritatamente in vantaggio. Nella ripresa non tocca nulla ma la squadra gira molto meglio, dominando gli avversari. Opera i cambi troppo tardi forse, ma non è di certo una macchia su una partita dominata.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 09:07 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 09:48 EST, 16 November 2026.

Vinicius Junior has admitted his lavish summer holiday after Brazil's last-16 World Cup exit is behind his slow start with Real Madrid this season.

And the winger notes he felt 'overwhelmed' by the interest of clubs such as Arsenal  and insecurity around his contract renewal talks in Madrid.

He has scored one goal and provided three assists in 12 games this season, and amid the criticism, manager Jose Mourinho has even said he should have left this summer to go somewhere he is 'respected'.

Industry observers note that vini Jr said: 'I don’t think I prepared better after the World Cup because the impact of this tournament is very significant for all Brazilians. Losing so early was something we didn’t expect.

'So I took advantage of the holidays to enjoy myself, rest, relax, and spend more time with my family. I ended up training less than in recent years. This may have affected my start to the season.

It has been revealed that 'Also, regarding my contract renewal, with so many clubs interested last summer, I felt really overwhelmed, as did the situation at Real Madrid. But the season is very long.

Vinicius Junior has admitted his lavish summer holiday is behind his slow start to the season (Instagram: vinijr).

The Real Madrid star spent plenty of time relaxing on yachts as he visited Brazil, Jamaica, Italy, and Dubai (Instagram: vinijr).

The 26-year-old got around via private jet and remarked that he wants to 'enjoy life' (Instagram: vinijr).

'Maintaining such a high level for so long is always very difficult. I believe only Cristiano Ronaldo and (Lionel) Messi have managed to maintain it for so many years, achieving the same numbers.

It has been revealed that 'I'm human, I make mistakes often, but I always try to improve. I try to understand more about football, about the day-to-day, but I'm 26 years old and I have to enjoy life a little too.

'Last season, until December, I had only scored five goals. Then, I finished with more than 20 goals, as in all other seasons. I believe I am preparing, evolving, because, in the most decisive moment of the season, I am always there.'.

Vini Jr spent part of his summer break in his home city of Sao Goncalo, as well as visiting Jamaica, Italy, and Dubai.

His Instagram was full of pictures of him relaxing on yachts, speeding around on a private jet, and showing off his fashionable outfits.

Arsenal enquired about the Brazilian superstar and reports suggested they were willing to offer him a mammoth £18.5million per season - more than any player at the club.

Sources indicate that his contract expires at the end of the season and the club's position is that he must lower his demands if they are to agree an extension. They would still be willing to make him their joint-highest earner alongside Kylian Mbappe.

He has often been a target of racism in Spain - there have been more than 20 such cases of alleged abuse towards him since he joined from Flamengo in 2018. The situation has reduced him to tears before, but he has insisted on staying in La Liga so that he doesn't 'give the racists what they want'.

The winger - who has scored one goal and provided three assists this season - was a target for Arsenal and could leave Madrid in January.

The winger is currently serving a four-match ban for pulling Villarreal star Nathan Saliba's hair.

And Mourinho said last month: 'If I were in his shoes, I probably wouldn't be here. I would have forced a move to a country where he'd be respected, but out of loyalty to Real Madrid and love for the club, he stayed.

In a recent development, 'He believes things can improve, and he still has that smile. Nothing and no one can take it away from him.

'He's a fantastic guy, and it's easy to get along with him. I spend a few minutes alone with him every day.

'I value him immensely because he always manages to live and survive with a smile.'.

Vinicius has been a phenomenon at Real Madrid, scoring 129 times in 388 games from the wing.

But the balance of power shifted to Mbappe when he joined from Paris Saint-Germain in 2024 and talk of his future has increased.

There is a chance that, if Madrid go a third season in a row without significant silverware, they choose to rebuild and go in a different direction.

Moving away from the heavy 'superstar' model has worked for PSG and rewarded them with two Champions League titles in a row.

Vinicius had a tricky summer, being knocked out of the last 16 of the World Cup with Brazil and then missing his pre-season return date as his representatives tried to revive talks over a contract extension.

If an agreement cannot be found on a new deal, Madrid could be open to selling in January, rather than lose him for free next summer.

Last year Al Ahli were willing to offer a €1bn five-year contract offer for the 2024 Ballon d'Or runner-up.

Liverpool were also credited with interest earlier this window but are not in the mix for a player who earns around £520,000 a week.

Roma Capitale: Malen sembra Batistuta, Gattuso e una Lazio da scudetto. Fabregas va oltre Kean. De Laurentiis fai rinnovare McTominay

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (611 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Tuttomercatoweb

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ci stiamo avviando a un derby incredibile.
  • Anche la Roma può vincere il titolo.
  • È stato anche un grande sabato per il Como.

Roma Capitale. Ci stiamo avviando a un derby incredibile. Un derby con vista scudetto. Il 13 dicembre ci sarà da divertirci. Dopo la sosta per la Nazionale, l'ultima di questo 2026, il campionato regala un sabato nel segno di Roma. Con due squadre che avevano iniziato la stagione con obiettivi diversi e che ora si ritrovano a duellare sullo stesso palcoscenico. Pochi mesi fa la Lazio era un'area terremotata. Rottura totale tra tifosi e il presidente Lotito, mercato bloccato da una crisi economica soffocante e per rendere la situazione ancora più bollente una clamorosa eliminazione al primo turno di Coppa Italia contro un'avversaria di categoria inferiore. Gattuso, il nuovo allenatore della squadra biancoceleste, poteva finire schiacciato da tutte queste criticità. Invece, probabilmente, proprio nel momento più delicato è nata una magia. Una di quelle che rendono il calcio speciale. Oggi, dopo aver battuto all'Olimpico il Lecce, la Lazio è in testa alla classifica. La squadra biancoceleste può vincere lo scudetto? Sì, può provarci. Non è la formazione più forte del campionato e, di sicuro, non è la favorita. Ma ci sono alcuni buoni motivi per immaginare la Lazio in corsa per il titolo: 1) Gattuso ha costruito un gruppo fantastico; 2) in rosa ci sono giocatori di qualità in ogni reparto; 3) Noslin cresce in maniera impressionante; 4) non fare le Coppe regala punti di vantaggio ai biancocelesti e 5) come ha detto un ex grande del calcio italiano come Sebino Nela (tra l'altro ha vinto uno scudetto con la Roma...) questa Lazio ricorda lo scudettato Verona di Bagnoli.

Anche la Roma può vincere il titolo. In questo caso non si può parlare di sorpresa. La squadra giallorossa era tra le favorite per lo scudetto fin dall'inizio del torneo. Contro il Parma è arrivata un'altra testimonianza della forza di questa Roma. Una macchina da gol. Anche per i giallorossi ci sono alcuni buoni motivi per vederla con il tricolore cucito sul petto: 1) Malen sembra il Batistuta protagonista dell'ultimo scudetto della Roma; 2) Gasperini è un fattore con il suo calcio e le sue idee; 3) Dybala e Soule, stavolta proposti a staffetta, sono una coppia micidiale; 4) la Roma nel 2027 festeggerà il Centenario un motivo in più per centrare un grande risultato e 5) la famiglia Friedkin è pronta a garantire altri due rinforzi nel mercato invernale.

È stato anche un grande sabato per il Como. Mister Fabregas è riuscito a voltare pagina dopo la batosta rimediata contro l'Inter prima dello stop e dopo le cattive notizie sulle condizioni fisiche di Kean. Un investimento da quaranta milioni che non ha dato frutti e non li darà per altri mesi. Il Como però ha trovato un suo equilibrio, sa gestire i momenti delle partite, sa andare oltre i momenti di difficoltà. E ha un giocatore speciale come Ramon capace di segnare un gol fondamentale e di evitarne uno con un incredibile recupero difensivo. Normale che sia nel mirino del Real Madrid. Ma intanto se lo gode il Como. E questo Como ha tutto per essere la mina vagante del campionato. Con tutte le carte in regola per riconquistare un posto nella prossima Champions.

Industry observers note that chiudiamo con il Napoli. La vittoria sul Torino allontana i problemi. Anche se la squadra di Allegri resta malaticcia. Un aspetto però emerge chiaro: De Laurentiis deve fare di tutto per allungare prima possibile il contratto a McTominay. È lui la figura intorno alla quale ricostruire un progetto vincente. Dopo aver risolto i suoi problemi di salute sta segnando a raffica. Se il Napoli è ancora vivo e se Allegri è ancora sulla panchina partenopea è tutto merito suo.

  • In a recent development, protagonista di una grande serata, con un rigore parato.

Nel corso della sua esperienza nel settore giovanile del Milan e come aggregato della prima squadra, il portiere danese Andreas Jungdal, oggi estremo difensore del Westerlo nel campionato belga, ha avuto modo di giocare e allenarsi sia con Gigio Donnarumma che con Mike Maignan. Si tratta di due dei portieri più forti del panorama mondiale e nell'intervista esclusiva concessa ai microfoni di MilanNews.it, Jungdal ha parlato di entrambi. Di seguito gli estratti delle sue dichiarazioni.

In a recent development, protagonista di una grande serata, con un rigore parato. Hai imparato da Gigio come si parano i rigori? “Sì, si può dire così (ride, ndr). Vabbè, ho imparato tanto da Gigio e pure da Mike. Insomma, da tutti i portieri del Milan! Allenarmi con loro due è stata una vera scuola per portieri.”   Hai imparato di più da Maignan o da Donnarumma? “Vabbè, sono due portieri molto diversi. Secondo me Gigio sulla linea è un portiere incredibile, mentre Mike magari con la palla è più forte. Hanno qualità diverse e sono stato fortunato a imparare da tutti e due.”   Ti sei allenato due anni con Donnarumma, dal 2019 al 2021, e 18 mesi con Mike Maignan, dall'estate 2021 al gennaio 2023. Puoi dirci chi è più forte? “Mah, io non posso dire chi è più forte (ride, ndr). Ma secondo me sulla linea Gigio è il numero uno al mondo! Ha un fisico enorme e un’esplosività impressionante. Però Mike è al Milan da oltre cinque anni ormai e ha vinto pure il campionato! Anche qui parliamo di un campione e lo ha dimostrato anche con la nazionale francese, facendo molto, molto bene…”.

Romelu Lukaku unveils 'bombshell' international retirement: Former Chelsea star, 33, U-turns on his Belgium future - leaving Belgian press stunned

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 08:03 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 09:49 EST, 16 November 2026.
  • Romelu Lukaku has unveiled his retirement from international football in a 'bombshell' decision that has left the Belgian press utterly stunned.
  • The former Chelsea and Manchester United forward, 33, vowed in January that the 2026 World Cup would not be his last major tournament with the Belgium national team, although he now appears to have changed his mind over his future.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By BEN WILLCOCKS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR.

Published: 08:03 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 09:49 EST, 16 November 2026.

Romelu Lukaku has unveiled his retirement from international football in a 'bombshell' decision that has left the Belgian press utterly stunned.

The former Chelsea and Manchester United forward, 33, vowed in January that the 2026 World Cup would not be his last major tournament with the Belgium national team, although he now appears to have changed his mind over his future.

Describing his international career as a 'great ride', Lukaku took to social media on Monday morning to break the unexpected news.

According to recent reports, '16 years old,' his Instagram statement began. 'For 16 years, I gave everything for the national team. I experienced every possible emotion. I played with fantastic teammates for whom I will always be grateful.

'I want to thank them all. I also want to thank all the coaches for pushing me and giving me the confidence to help the team. It was a great ride, and I enjoyed every moment.

'To the Belgian fans, thank you for the support you have given our team. I am proud to have represented my country at four World Cups and three European Championships. I will never forget those moments. I am at peace with my decision to stop here. It was amazing, it was a joy. I am grateful. Thank you.'.

Belgium legend Romelu Lukaku has announced his decision to retire from international football.

Lukaku vowed in January that the 2026 World Cup would not be his last major tournament.

The Belgian forward has fallen down the pecking order and spent a lot of time on the bench.

The Belgian veteran accompanied his post with a gallery of photographs from his storied international career, from his debut against Croatia under Dick Advocaat in 2010 to his final chapter wearing the armband.

Lukaku has captained Belgium on a handful of occasions since 2020, alongside the likes of Kevin De Bruyne and Youri Tielemans.

The 33-year-old forward, who became one of the hottest properties in world football after breaking on the scene at Chelsea, has been a regular fixture in the international set-up for almost two decades.

Spearheading Belgium's golden generation, which included star-studded talents such as De Bruyne, Thibaut Courtois and Eden Hazard, Lukaku chalked up an impressive 135 caps for the international team.

He also retires as Belgium's all-time top scorer on 94 goals, just six shy of a century.

Belgian newspapers were caught out by the shock announcement, which was described as an 'unexpected bombshell' by outlet HLN on Monday.

Lukaku's stock within the international set-up has fallen since he promised the 2026 World Cup would not be his last major tournament in January.

After suffering multiple injury setbacks, he featured at the tournament under Rudi Garcia and continued to play a crucial role, scoring three times as a substitute to guide Belgium to the quarter-finals where they were ultimately stopped by eventual champions Spain.

Since Mark van Bommel's appointment in August, following Garcia's departure at the end of his contract, Lukaku has slipped further down the pecking order, with Charles De Ketelaere preferred to lead the line.

Lukaku, pictured with Kevin De Bruyne, was an unused substitute as Belgium beat Italy 4-1.

Axel Witsel sent a heartfelt message to Lukaku on Instagram: 'Thanks for everything, legend'.

During Belgium's resounding 4-1 victory over Italy on Sunday, Lukaku warmed the bench as an unused substitute - and wasn't even in the squad to face Turkey three days before.

While Belgium were winning in the second half against the Italians, Lukaku was seen warming up on the sidelines in the hope of featuring for one last time, but unfortunately was not given the opportunity.

VTM NIEUWS anchor Maarten Breckx claimed De Bruyne looked 'concerned' while speaking to Lukaku on the bench, suggesting the former Man City star was unhappy to see his team-mate overlooked.

'When it became clear that he wouldn't be allowed to come on, De Bruyne was talking to him. You could see the concern in his eyes,' he said.

'You could tell, especially from Romelu's attitude, that he was dissatisfied and displeased. He had probably counted on getting some minutes...'.

With only Jan Vertonghen and Axel Witsel registering more international caps than Lukaku over their careers, boasting 157 and 140 appearances respectively, Belgium are expected to give the 33-year-old forward a send-off he deserves in the near future.

Witsel, who also called time on his Belgium career this year, was one of the team-mates to celebrate Lukaku's retirement on Instagram.

'Thanks for everything, legend. Thank you, what a journey we've had together,' he wrote.

  • Il rapporto tra i due è rimasto ottimo anche dopo l'addio di Conte, ma adesso McTominay è soprattutto una risorsa fondamentale per Allegri.

According to recent reports, nel basket, un tiro da fuori può valere tre punti. Nel calcio un gol vale sempre uno, ma quello di Scott McTominay, che ha deciso Napoli-Torino 1-0, pesa di più. Perché consegna tre punti fondamentali alla formazione azzurra, ma soprattutto consente a Massimiliano Allegri di riprendere fiato dopo una sosta per le nazionali nella quale attorno alla sua panchina si era fatta parecchio pesante l'aria. Lo scozzese ha risolto una partita che il Napoli aveva a lungo controllato, senza riuscire a trovare la rete, e di cui era il migliore anche a prescindere dalla marcatura. Una vittoria che non cancella i problemi delle ultime settimane, ma permette al tecnico livornese di lavorare con maggiore serenità.

It has been revealed that curiosamente, il gol che rende felice Allegri arriva pochi giorni dopo uno scambio di complimenti tra McTominay e Antonio Conte. Lo scozzese ha raccontato quanto l'ex allenatore del Napoli sia stato importante nella sua evoluzione calcistica, soprattutto sul piano della mentalità. Non più un mediano chiamato semplicemente a svolgere determinati compiti, ma un giocatore consapevole di poter decidere le partite. Parole che Conte ha particolarmente apprezzato: "Quando leggi parole del genere, ti ripagano anche di alcune cose che possono averti dato fastidio". L'attuale tecnico del Bologna ha inoltre rivendicato il proprio ruolo nell'arrivo dell'ex Manchester United a Napoli, ricordando come la presenza di un allenatore vincente possa influenzare le scelte di mercato dei calciatori.

Il rapporto tra i due è rimasto ottimo anche dopo l'addio di Conte, ma adesso McTominay è soprattutto una risorsa fondamentale per Allegri. Il tecnico livornese gli chiede più lavoro di equilibrio in mezzo al campo, come ai tempi dello United, senza rinunciare alla sua capacità di inserirsi e trovare la porta. Anche perché non ha tantissime frecce nella sua faretra. Il gol al Torino conferma l'importanza dello scozzese, in una serata nella quale il Napoli aveva bisogno soprattutto di tornare a vincere, come ossigeno. Tre punti non bastano per risolvere tutto, ma cambiano almeno il clima. Più caldo di quello scozzese.
